This town combines the atmosphere of an old-fashioned European resort with wide sandy beaches and scenic natural panoramas that have made it one of the country's popular holiday destinations.

Piriápolis is closely tied to its founder, Francisco Piria, who envisioned a resort inspired by European seaside towns in the early 20th century. Traces of that era remain in its historic architecture, the elegant Hotel Argentino and the Rambla de los Argentinos waterfront promenade, a pleasant place to stroll while admiring the ocean.

The hills surrounding the town give it a special charm. A climb to Cerro San Antonio reveals panoramic views of the coast, harbor and tiled roofs, while a trip to Cerro del Toro offers natural scenery and viewpoints. In the warmer months, visitors come for the beaches, seaside walks and welcoming cafés serving local cuisine.

Compared with bustling Punta del Este, Piriápolis has a quieter, more intimate atmosphere. It is an inviting place to spend a few days enjoying the sea air, an unhurried pace and the combination of architectural heritage and natural beauty.

Piriápolis shows Uruguay at its most romantic: an endless ocean, the charm of a historic seaside resort and hills with unforgettable coastal views.

Pisac lies in the Sacred Valley of the Incas near Cusco. Its archaeological complex includes agricultural terraces, residential structures and ceremonial spaces. The buildings occupy the hillsides and follow the surrounding terrain, with sweeping views of the valley from certain points.

The modern settlement is known for its handicraft market. Walking through it adds an introduction to local products and traditional craftsmanship to a visit among the ancient structures. Pisac reveals two connected sides of the Sacred Valley: stone architecture and agriculture from the Inca period, and the culture of communities that continue to thrive beside the monuments.

Pisco is a town on Peru's coast that prospered and became famous for the excellent-quality spirit produced there from particularly juicy, sweet grapes.

## Holidays in Pisco

### Pisco — an Inca center and the birthplace of vodka!

This vodka has been known around the world since time immemorial, and today the Pisco brand has become a symbol of tradition and a source of pride for Peruvians. Paracas National Reserve lies 22 km from the city of Pisco and covers 335,000 hectares. The reserve consists of deserts, beaches, islands and coastal cliffs washed by the Pacific Ocean. Flamingos, pelicans, dolphins, fur seals, cormorant colonies and a great variety of fish and crustaceans are protected here in their natural habitats. The Pisco area is also of historical and archaeological interest as one of the most developed centers of the ancient Inca civilization.

## Playas del Este — paradise beaches!

Surrounded by coconut palms, these white-sand beaches begin at Bacuranao, 18 km from Havana, and continue east through Tarará, El Mégano, Santa María del Mar and Boca Ciega to Guanabo.

## Playas del Este — a beach lover's paradise!

Scattered like a string of pearls along the eastern edge of the capital, the beaches are known as the "Blue Ring." They are very popular with tourists and Havana residents alike because they are so close to the city. Warm seawater in shades of blue and emerald washes the shores and is so clear that underwater visibility reaches 20–30 meters. Tides here are gentle, strong currents are absent, and in many places coral reefs protect the coast from large waves.

## Playa del Carmen — a resort town!

Playa del Carmen is a city in the Mexican state of Quintana Roo, located in the heart of the Riviera Maya resort area on the Yucatán Peninsula, along the Caribbean Sea.

Palm-fringed beaches abound, while coral reefs stretch along the coast. Lively pedestrian Fifth Avenue runs beside the shore, offering visitors shops, restaurants and nightlife for every taste, from bustling dance clubs to bars with a relaxed atmosphere.

## Things to do in Playa del Carmen!

The coast attracts divers, while its magnificent beaches are ideal for simply enjoying a peaceful break. Famous Fifth Avenue is the main street and entertainment center. In the evening, you can sample tequila in the bars or dance salsa all night in discos and clubs. Playa del Carmen is close to strikingly beautiful places such as Xcaret and Xel-Há, as well as the ancient Maya city of Tulum.
